_comment: Per-project harness config. Copy to your project root as hydra-agents.json and edit. All paths are relative to the project root (checked in, portable). This example carries Hydra's own values.
_sessionPrefix_comment: Optional. Machine-global prefix for tmux session / agent names, so two projects on one host don't collide on `staging` / `feature_NNN_*`. Defaults to the repo name from issueRepo + '-' (here: 'hydra-'). Override only if the repo name is awkward. Branch/worktree names stay unprefixed.
_standardizedBranches_comment: Optional. Space-separated set of branch names that exist on EVERY machine (staging, …) and so must be machine-qualified in the session/agent name to stay distinct across a multi-machine fleet — e.g. staging -> 'hydra-staging-<machine1>' / 'hydra-staging-<machine2>' (suffix from `hostname -s`). Issue branches (feature_NNN_*) are already unique and stay unqualified. Defaults to 'staging'.
_stagingPeers_comment: Optional. The exact session names of this project's staging sessions on OTHER machines: the only off-machine recipients a staging session may message (docs/cross-worktree-messages.md § Project isolation). Use the name other machines resolve, which is the Remote Control label; claude-remote launches use the same string for both. Never fill this from a ListAgents listing. Example values are placeholders.
_denyListAgents_comment: Optional, default "true": spawn and recovery add a ListAgents deny to each worktree's .claude/settings.local.json, so agents address peers by computed name only. Set "false" only where user-level settings already deny it.
_isolateWorkers_comment: Optional, default "true": confine worker sessions to their machine (with Claude Code, isolatePeerMachines in each worker worktree's settings.local.json). This is a per-machine choice, so leave it "true" here and override it on a machine that runs only public projects, in hydra-agents.local.json (gitignored, beside this file) or with HYDRA_AGENTS_ISOLATE_WORKERS=false. Set it back to "true" when private projects share the machine.
